subject.title: fix(agents): avoid symlink-follow in auth.json bootstrap

question: Should OpenClaw permanently own the no-final-path-chmod and descriptor-mode hardening wrapper, or should that guarantee be added and released in `@openclaw/fs-safe` before this security fix lands?
rationale: Both routes can address the observed auth bootstrap vulnerability, but only maintainers can choose the lasting ownership and public dependency contract for shared atomic replacement.

options.title: Move the guarantee upstream
options.body: Add and release a supported fs-safe option or behavior for exact descriptor-based modes without final-path chmod, then simplify OpenClaw back to delegation.

options.title: Approve the local wrapper
options.body: Accept `src/infra/replace-file.ts` as the documented OpenClaw owner for this narrowly scoped hardening and retain its async, sync, fallback, and queue-order regression coverage.

recommendation.title: Move the guarantee upstream
recommendation.body: Add and release a supported fs-safe option or behavior for exact descriptor-based modes without final-path chmod, then simplify OpenClaw back to delegation.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is specifically a security ownership and dependency-boundary decision requested from this review group.
